utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do remember that reference, but I really don't remember that person's presence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, you did tell us that you didn't remember that person's presence, but it is a document that you signed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, probably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just to correct, this document is Exhibit 581, not 582.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, we came to that same conclusion. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: P02300. Yes, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. May the witness please be shown P02294.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, I know you did not author this document, but at the top of it, it says: "The General Staff of the Army," is that correct, and it's a bulletin?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: That's what it says. I've never seen the document before, though.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'd like you to turn to page 4 in English, and 3 in B/C/S, please. One moment. Yes. The part where it begins: "The 3rd Corps SVB ...," do you see that section, sir? Do you see where it says "SVB," sir? The paragraphs are not numbered, but I believe it's -- I have it marked as page 3 of the B/C/S version, and it starts with "SVB, 3rd Corps." It's right there. Can you tell us what that paragraph is about, sir?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may be of assistance, it's the next page in the Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, does that paragraph refer to again two doctors, one nurse, and 11 Bosniaks?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know what the source was for this particular piece of information, and I can't confirm it, either, with the exception of what it says about the 11 Bosniaks, but that's about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Correct. But this -- the 11 Bosniaks that are referred to here as being captured, is this the same 11 Bosniaks from all the previous reports that we've just looked at?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: I assume so. I never heard of another incident like this again anywhere else, I mean, about the 11 Bosnians being captured.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And at the end of that paragraph, and it's on the next page in English, page 5 in English, the last sentence of the paragraph with reference to the El Mujahid Detachment, it specifically states here, does it not, that the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we be shown the next page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: It's at the top, okay, right there, the last sentence of that paragraph, first paragraph, where it says: "All the captured aggressor soldiers are being held by the El Mudjahedin Detachment soldiers and so far they do not allow anyone access to these prisoners."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: That's what the document says, sir?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And was that your experience as well, that you didn't have access to them?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, apart from the situation that I described.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd ask that this document be admitted in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Sorry. I have a question to you regarding the destiny of this document. Where did it go? What was the bulletin, and to whom was it addressed, and was it passed further up?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes, the Presiding Judge explains to me that this is a bulletin within the army, but my question would still be: How far up does it go?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I believe another witness has spoken about these bulletins. I believe it was Mr. Berbic that -- he -- it goes to the General Staff of the Army, the Command Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And just for the record, could we look at the last page of the document to see whose name is there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The name at the end of the document?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Just who submitted this document, whose name is on the document.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What's the name there, Madam Sartorio?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: It's on the right-hand side of the English page, and it may be further down on the Bosnian. I have actually a different -- I must have a different translation. I have a different translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you expect a name --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- Madam Sartorio --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- on the bulletin?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I will withdraw that question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may, if this is the same page of the Bosnian and the same page of the English, then the English contains an addition that we do not seem to come across in the Bosnian, each of the pages were certified, or maybe I just don't see it on the screen. If we could see the Bosnian version in its entirety, perhaps. Right, the translation of the stamp. My apologies, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, it explains the stamp. Thank you. Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Next Exhibit number 582.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May the witness be shown, please, P02482. And can we go to the very last page of this document, please. And the last page in English as well, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, is that your signature on the document in front of you on the Bosnian copy?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And now may we go back to the first page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: While we're getting there, could you explain to the Chamber what this document is?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document painting a picture of the security situation that prevailed in the units of the 35th Division. It is being submitted to the chief of Security Service -- Military Security Service of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And what is the date of the document, sir, and to whom did the document go? Excuse me, you just answered that. What was the date of the document? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: The 30th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. I would like to go to page 20 in the English, and all I can give you is the ERN for the Bosnian copy. There are no page numbers. 0414-9687, if you can find it. It's the paragraph on the bottom on the B/C/S, and if we could bring it up and try to enlarge it as much as possible, please, for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to ask you a couple of questions, since you -- did you write this report?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Probably not on my own. My associates helped me along.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: But, again, if you signed the report, would you -- wouldn't you have adopted it as being correct or accurate?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, if we read this first paragraph, you're discussing the El Mujahedin unit, as it's called, acting independently and not respecting the -- is that the control-and-command system of the army?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And was this a concern of the security organ of the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and we kept issuing warnings about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And then the next -- we're still in the first paragraph, but the next sentence it talks about: "The unit has completed all assigned military tasks." Is that what that says?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: The unit has achieved certain military successes. At the same time, there was a backlash that came from this, which is something that I spoke about earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Right. But I think you jumped one sentence ahead. The sentence at the end of the first paragraph starting with: "Since October 1994 ...," is it in your -- the original Bosnian copy, does it say the unit completed all assigned military tasks; is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, then it also talks about -- it uses "military successes achieved." Is that also referred to in this paragraph -- or in the next paragraph?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now I'd like you to go to the last sentence of this long paragraph, starting with: "The security organ of the 35th Division ..." It states that you -- that your security organ of the 35th Division registered all incidents, but no energetic measures have been taken." Is that what that says?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I ask that this document be admitted in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 583.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May I have one more moment, Your Honour, please. Thank you. Thank you, Your Honours, for the indulgence. May the witness be shown P02482. Oh, sorry, I keep going to the -- sorry. P02574.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: But before I get to that: Sir, other than this incident -- other than the capture of the POWs in July of 1995, did you ever hear about another capture of VRS soldiers? In particular -- well, yes, another capture. Did you ever hear of anything?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: When combat operations started in Operation Farz, there were instances when prisoners were taken, and there were many rumours about prisoners. But I didn't see them and I can't confirm how many, who captured them, where, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: But you did hear rumours?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were rumours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you tell us what -- specifically what those rumours were?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, quite simply that the Serb soldiers were surrendering, that prisoners were being taken, and that the Serb forces were in disarray.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: But as assistant commander for the security organ of the 35th Division, did you not make attempts to follow up on these rumours?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we tried as much as we could, and we reported on all that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Then why didn't you succeed? Why couldn't you see those prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All the prisoners who were brought in by the military police of the BH Army were taken to the military detention centre in Zavidovici and then they were immediately transferred to Zenica, and access was possible only to those prisoners. I didn't see any other prisoners. But as I already indicated, we just heard rumours about them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So are you saying that you actually did have a chance to see the prisoners who were handed over to the military police, but that there were other prisoners that you did not have a chance to talk to; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for the former, I had an opportunity to see them, but as for the latter, the only knowledge that I had was based on the rumours. I didn't have any opportunity to see them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I understand. Let's just have a look at the first group of prisoners, that is to say, those prisoners who were handed over to the military police. And you said that for those, you did have a chance to see them. My question is here: Did you actually talk to all of the prisoners who were taken by the military police and transferred to Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not to all of them. Those were small groups. They came in small groups, two to three prisoners, so I can't give you the exact number, the total number, but the military police brought in those smaller groups of prisoners and then took them on to Zenica, but that would be 10 to 12 prisoners in total at the most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. So I understand that you did talk to most of them and you could have talked to them if you would have wanted to, because you could have gone to Zenica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was not my duty to go to Zenica and to talk with them there. They were dealt with by other organs there. My duty was simply to forward them to Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Very well. But the interest is mostly concerned with the other group of prisoners, those that you only heard rumours about, and my question still stands, namely: Why did you not have a chance to see them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We didn't know where they were. We didn't know who had captured them. We didn't know how many of them there were. We didn't know where they were. We simply didn't know what place they were kept in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But to follow up on Ms. Sartorio's question, what did the rumours say about where they were, and who had taken them, and how many there were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, there were just rumours about many prisoners, but nothing specific, no specific information that could lead us to the place or give us an idea of the actual number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Over to you, Ms. Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, just a second. I don't know whether this is a problem of interpretation or is there a misspeaking on your part. At page 56, line 15, you say: "My duty was simply to forward them to Zenica." And I just want to confirm with you, did you forward them to Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All the prisoners that were brought in by the military police, so that was primarily the task of the military police to do so. They --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just answer my question. Did you forward them to Zenica, you? You said: "My duty was simply to forward them to Zenica." Now, did you forward them to Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I may have misspoken. It was not my duty, it was the duty of the military police, and they were all forwarded to Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But when they were taken by the police, military police, to Zavidovici before they were transferred to Zenica, was it not your duty to go and interview them, like you went and interviewed these others in Livade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A brief interview was conducted while they were awaiting transportation to Zenica, just the basic information was obtained from them, and this was done for the most part by the intelligence organ from the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But then what about the security organ? You are responsible for security. The Intelligence were taking intelligence. You want to look after security.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We didn't really take any measures in this respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're talking about -- when you say "we," you mean the security organ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the Security Service organ.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Both of the 35th Division and of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I'm talking about only the 35th Division, the organ there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Over to you, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Excuse me, my voice. We are on P02574. I believe it's up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, I know that this document is not from your security organ, but it's from the intelligence organ. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And were you still in your position as assistant commander for Security on the 11th of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but that was already the stage where I was handing over my duties to somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Right. But on the English version, please, if we could go over -- make the page --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Can we just scroll down, rather. We just want to read what is in this page; right?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I wanted you to do. I'd like you to read this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, sir, does this document talk about some VRS soldiers being captured, or being in custody, or taken over?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't write this document, but as far as I'm able to see, it does refer to some prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Are these the prisoners about which you heard rumours?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I really can't comment on it. I didn't write this.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Right. But if you were -- but if the assistant commander for Intelligence is writing and knows about this, wouldn't it -- wouldn't it have been something that would have come to the security organ?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. This is the first time that I see this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honours, may we mark this for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is marked for identification. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be MFI 584.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Pending what, exactly?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: For another witness to comment on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution has no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You did very well. You just went by four minutes over your time, in terms of time. Is that then a convenient time? We'll take a break and come back at half past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Imamovic. My name is Vasvija Vidovic, and today I will be asking you some questions on behalf of General Rasim Delic. In the cross-examination, you can quite often respond to my questions with a "yes" or "no," and in order to save time I would like to ask you to do so, to say "yes" or "no." If you feel that you have to elaborate further, please do so. Likewise, we have a lot of problems with interpretation, and we have to make an effort to speak as slow as possible. And in light of the fact that we speak the same language, could you please make a small pause after my question before you start your answer, so that the transcript reflects everything that is said. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To save us some time, I would like to ask the witness to be shown Exhibit 583.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Imamovic, you will remember that you've seen this document just now, and you will remember that the Prosecutor asked you about a portion of it that refers to the El Mudjahedin Detachment, the briefing about this detachment. I will go back to this in the course of my cross-examination, but now I would like us to look at the same document from a different angle to see what its contents are. Could the witness please be shown page 6 of this document in Bosnian and page 8 in the English version. Could the Bosnian version be zoomed in just a little bit so that the witness is able to read it. Sir, do you agree that this part of the document talks about the establishment of staffing levels and the level of training in the Security Service and the military police units? This is the document originating from your division. You said you worked in that division when the Prosecutor asked you that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the data contained here, the number of officers, non-commissioned officers, and then could you please look at what is written below this column, below this chart, if I may call it that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could you zoom in a little bit for us to see the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I can't see the figures here in English, but the witness will assist us by reading the relevant portions in the Bosnian version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you agree that it says here that in the Security Department in the 35th Division, there are 31 officers?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can see that? You can see that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you agree that it is explained further, below that, that only four of them have a university degree; do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you agree with me that military security, by its very nature, is such that all the military security officers, in order to be able to perform their duties properly, should have -- should be graduates from the military academy or have a university degree, in light of the sensitivity and complexity of the job?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And if I may add, not just a university degree or military academy, but a number of specialised courses that one needs to attend in order to be able to perform this job properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which column are you talking about, the column that has "31" in --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm speaking about the column where it says: "The manning levels for the personnel." That's the fifth column in this chart. It says here the staffing levels, and then it says "31", but it appears to me that there's nothing of the sort in the English text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's true, there's nothing of the sort in English, but the heading of that column, in the English, reads "Recruited," and you're talking about security. That's my problem. Now, I'm just wondering whether the translation is the same thing, is the same, is correct. And if it is not correct, how are we to go about this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there's something else missing. Could we please scroll down in the English version. Actually, the previous page in the English version, let us try to clarify that. Perhaps that is on the previous page. Could you scroll down? Your Honours, you can see the heading here where it says: "Establishment manning level and training of the Military Security Service and the military police units." This is item number two in the Bosnian version that you can see up here, and could we now go to the next page in the English version and could we look at the very beginning of this page. Fine. Your Honours, I was talking about the first -- the fifth column, where it says "Recruited." At the beginning you see where it says "Officers." I think have you that in the English version, too. So you can see here, in the fifth column --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand, Madam Vidovic, and do bear with me. I can only read the English. You have the advantage of being able to read B/C/S and English. And I'm saying I hear you talk to the witness about the number of security officers who were employed in the division, and you are saying there are 31. And I'm saying the heading that is number 5 in the English is not headed "Security," it's headed "Recruited." So then I get lost. I want to know, how do you determine that column number 5 talks about security? And it's not your fault, it's the fault of the document or my fault.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, let me try to clarify this and make it simple.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you agree that this table shows the establishment manning levels and training in the Military Security Service and the military police units in the 35th Division? Let's first establish that.

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, and if I may add --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm with you, I'm with you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the Trial Chamber now understands this, so there's no need for us to dwell on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What I asked you, and I have to apologise now, we really don't have that much time, Witness, only four of the officers had a university degree; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And if I may add, perhaps they didn't have an appropriate university degree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And could you now look at the text just below this table and the fifth sentence from above. Do you agree that it says here that only one security organ from the 35th Division used to work in the SVB of the former JNA? On this basis, I infer that you -- your Military Security Service lacked experience, with the exception of this one man in the 35th Division. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Given the circumstances, these were the only people we had.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. And you didn't have personnel who had undergone training for military security, I mean the military academy, with the specialty in military security?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. If I may clarify, those were mostly military security officers who had not had any training for that kind of a job. Those were mostly recruits who had been mobilised, who worked in the furniture factory, because we were all from that area, and they were appointed to those posts by mere chance, and they tried to do as good a job as they could.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you personally never went to the military academy. You had never performed any security tasks before you took up this post; right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true, I did not hold a degree from the military academy, and I was appointed to this post overnight, as it were, and even unbeknownst to me I was appointed, because it was somebody's assessment that I should take that job.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You don't have a degree in law, you don't have a police degree, do you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What do you have a degree in?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Political sciences.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the bottom of the page now. Do you agree that what it says is this: "The General Staff of the Army made 13 members take courses," and it is my understanding that the security organ of the 3rd Corps organised two seminars where almost everyone from your organ was involved or attended. Do you agree that the higher-ranking commands, although the circumstances were difficult and there was a war on, did their best to train their personnel?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we now turn to page 2 of this document, please. The English is all right. It's the last paragraph of the English that we want to look at, and then it continues from there. The next page of the Bosnian, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, please, look at the first three paragraphs of this page, especially the first part referring to the means available to the Military Security Department of the 35th division. Is this an error or am I reading it correctly? You only had a single camera and a tape-recorder, and that was all the equipment you had; is that right? That's all the equipment you had?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, unfortunately, that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Next page in the English, please. Next page in English. So, Witness, again we see here some talk of courses being organised by the General Staff and by Security, by the 3rd Corps Security. You agree, you agree? Let me ask you something else now. The higher-level commands tried to perform some sort of training, they tried to train their security officers. Do you agree that at those training sessions, they would also familiarise their officers with the rules governing their work, the work of the Security Service?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Those were crash courses, because that's all the circumstances ever allowed. They would normally boil down to the fundamentals, including the various regulations governing the work of security officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You agree that there was a regulation called "Rules Governing the Work of the Military Security Service"?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also Rules Governing the Work of Military Police?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that those rules were made available to the Military Security Service and its officers throughout the territory under the control of the army, including your own area?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to show the witness D566 at this point in time. For the record, these are rules governing the work of the Military Security Service in the Armed Forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you see this is a document adopted by the Presidency on the 11th of September, 1992, do you not? I do believe, furthermore, that you, as a member of the Security Service, had an opportunity to obtain a copy of this document and read through it. Would I be right in assuming that? I don't mean this particular copy; the Rules in general.

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like the witness to look at page 3 of the Bosnian and page 3 in the English. That is just the portion we are looking for.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, read item 1, please. This is about the area of competence of the Military Security Service. Please read it for yourself. You may be familiar with this already. Let me ask you this now. Have you read it? The Military Security Service is in charge of state security tasks within the armed forces, the objective being to offer adequate protection to military units, including Staff Commands, units, and any institutions belonging to the armed forces. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The objective is to protect unit Commands and to protect any activities to do with the use of these units in a bid to prevent other threats to units from inside the armed forces. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So I am right to believe that the Military Security Service dealt with members of the armed forces as well as those working against the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that it would be erroneous to assume that the purview of the Military Security Service only had to do with an area of responsibility in a purely territorial sense? In other words, it would be erroneous to assume that a certain organ of the Military Security Service was in charge of investigating everything that was happening in a certain area; right? They only investigate things to do with units of the army or something that is against the army; right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. If I may add, anything else that goes on in an area is the job of other bodies rather than Military Security.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mean civilian police, right, for example, protecting private property and civilians?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, State Security Service.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: State Security Service, which is a part of the Ministry of the Interior; right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Part of the government, if you like, not the army; State Security Service?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, these are the other bodies that would have been in charge.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Jurisdiction over persons not members of the army, on the condition that they weren't committing a crime against the army, that wasn't something that was within the purview of the Military Security Service; this was something for the civilian police to deal with, right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, under normal circumstances that is precisely the way it should work.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Be that as it may, do you agree that the tasks of the Military Security Service are defined in detail in the document before us?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that one of the tasks was to create conditions for documenting any war crimes to the fullest extent possible? Your Honours, if we could please move to the next page of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Maybe for the record we could ensure that it is reflected -- there it comes. Sorry, I didn't see the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I did ask the question, but it was not recorded. I asked you about a particular task for the Military Security Service. It had to do with creating conditions for documenting any war crimes to the fullest extent possible, or any other crimes, for that matter. Do you agree that this was within the purview of the Military Security Service?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, can the witness now please be shown page 6 of the Bosnian. The reference in English is page 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please focus on item 8, "Control of the Military Security Service." Do you agree that item 8 envisages this: "Members of the Military Security Service shall be directly subordinated to the commanding officer of the command, staff, unit or institution in which they serve." Is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have a number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 585.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now please look at D567.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, these are Rules Governing the Work of the Military Police of the Armed Forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. You see that this was adopted in September 1992, do you not? The Military Security Service, in the field, knew about this document, didn't they, and they acted in compliance with it, didn't they? Is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please go to page 6 of the Bosnian, the English reference being page 5. Could we scroll the Bosnian version down, please. Yes, that's right, thank you. The English is fine. I'm talking about the paragraph entitled "Command and Control of the Military Police." Please look at item 7. It reads: "Command and control of the military police is exercised by the commanding officer ..." Please now if we could turn to the next page of the Bosnian version. The English version should be all right, I think. At the top of the page, please. Do you agree that the rule also envisaged this, that: "Command and control of the military police should be exercised by the commanding officer in which a particular -- a commanding officer of the unit to which a particular military police unit belongs;" right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can we please explain what this means, exercising command and control of the military police, in a purely technical sense, if you can help us with that. If not, please do so. What is the role of the security organ in terms of technical guidance or command and control?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: The role of the security organ, in terms of technical control, comes down to coordinating the work of MP units, training these units for their day-to-day assignments. Also providing technical assistance during the actual implementation of these assignments would be included. No decisions, however, can be taken on how the military police is used.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That was my next question, Witness, as a matter of fact. Would I be right to assume that any decisions on the combat use of the military police were taken by the commander of whichever unit the MP contingent happened to be part of; right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 586.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you will agree with me, won't you, you were in touch with the military police, or rather perhaps you can help us with this. Is it not true that the MPs were sometimes used by various commanders in ways that didn't serve a particular purpose or perhaps in ways that were not in keeping with the regulations?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Indeed. If I may elaborate.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: By all means, please, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: There were certain situations where commanders enlisted the assistance of the MPs along the front lines as marksmen, and the Military Security Service did issue warnings and alert the relevant bodies about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I'm about to show you another document, D568. Before you look at this, Witness, it's true, isn't it, that security organs complained to higher-ranking commands about this sort of use that the MPs were put to? You personally, in fact, wrote certain letters requesting that the military police be used in a more purpose-oriented manner. I'm not talking about this document. I'm talking in general terms.

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Can you now please look at the document in front of you. Do you agree that this is an order called "Intended Use of the Military Police," and it was sent to the commanders of the 35th Division, the 37th Division and to independent units on the 12th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the corps commander notices the problem of the MPs not being used in the way they are intended to be used, and through this document he bans any such use of the military police that was not in keeping with the rules and orders that the MPs henceforth be used only in keeping with the rules? Your Honours, if we could please pull the English version down a little so that you may be able to follow. Thank you. The lower half of the document, the English. That's right. So this was the order that was sent to the 35th Division by the Corps Command; right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And if I may add something.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: The handwritten portion, that's my handwriting. I write here that this should be forwarded to all the bodies in all the brigades and battalions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have the next page in the English, and eventually I'll return to this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So my understanding is you received this order and you passed it along to all the brigades and battalions on the ground. Right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is my instruction to my associates concerning the implementation of this order.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, can we please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 587.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a member of the Military Security Service, perhaps you can help us with this. You were asked certain questions by the OTP, and you mentioned units including the 35th Division and lower-level units too, these units were familiar with the provisions of International Law of War, they knew about the provisions enshrined in the Geneva Conventions, and so on and so forth, and how any POWs were to be treated; right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this point in time, D569, that's the document that I want the witness to see next.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you agree this is a document produced by the 3rd Corps Command, dated the 27th of May, 1995. It says: "Treatment of POWs, defectors, persons exchanged and expelled from their areas." This was sent to division and independent unit commanders. Can you please look at this particular page of this document. I will give you some time to do that, sir. Do you agree about this: The 3rd Corps Command here defines exactly what the treatment should be of any POWs, and they were adamant that any POWs should be treated in keeping with the laws of Bosnia and Herzegovina and with the resolutions signed by Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that not right, sir?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, very much so, and I believe I have spoken about these procedures when prompted to do so by the OTP earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the reception of POWs, selection of POWs, opening files on POWs; right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Finally, written reports were to be submitted to the assistant commander for Security of the 3rd Corps; right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Let's move on to the next page of this document, please. And the English, too. If you look at number 14, the 3rd Corps Commander says that the commanders of divisions and so on are responsible for a consistent implementation of this order; right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You, who were in the division, forwarded this order to the units that were on the ground; right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number 588.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit 396, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You gave evidence today about issues, among other things, to do with the resubordination of the El Mujahid Detachment to the 35th Division. Please look at this document. You may never have seen it before, for all I know, but I do want you to look at some facts here. Resubordination on the 2nd of June, 1995. This is a 3rd Corps order, as you see. Item 1, "Resubordinate the El Mujahid Detachment to the 35th Division Command," and focus on the specific figure there, between 350 and 400 fighters. Could we scroll the English down a little, please. Next page, please. Thank you. You see the figure mentioned there, the El Mujahid, between 350 and 400 fighters, and then observation posts, Dolac, Blizna, Liz [phoen], Vis, Paljenik, this is the area of responsibility of the 35th Division, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Your Honours, could we please move to the next page of this document in the Bosnian so that we can tell exactly when it was dispatched. Scroll down a little, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: There is a handwritten note, "35th Division, KoV," and the time appears to be 2109; right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please keep that in mind. There is another quote there in reference to the time it was dispatched to the El Mujahid Detachment. Still on the same topic, I wish to show I was different document now, but could we put this one away first, and I would like the witness to look at D570. Witness, first of all, I would like to ask you the following: You were in the Command of the 35th Division. Do you know Hajrudin Djelmic, a man by that name?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: That was the officer in the operations and training organ at the 35th Division Command.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. And who is Almir Husic?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: I think he was a soldier who actually worked on the computer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. And do you recognise the signature here?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: I think that this is the signature of the commander of the 35th Division, Fadil Hasanagic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. Could you please look at this document. The date is the 2nd of June, 1995, and right below it it says operational time, 1530 hours; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is a document that was drafted on the same date as the previous one, the only difference being that this one was written several hours before the other one? The previous one was sent from the division at around 2100 hours, and here we have the time as 1530 on the same date; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please read this document to yourself --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before that, Madam Vidovic, can we just place on the record that the English translation is actually dated a day earlier, and I don't know which is the mistake. I guess the mistake must be the English. It couldn't have been translated before it was written.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, obviously, obviously. The date is quite clear here. It's the 2nd of June. I apologise. I never even noticed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are right, but the English translation is --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will correct that, Your Honours. In fact, we first had a very, very poor copy at our disposal, and then we asked for a better copy from the archive, and that is probably why this error occurred. It was not legible. But now we have a very good copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I asked you a little while ago to keep in mind the elements from the order of the 3rd Corps. Do you agree that this document -- apparently in this document, on the 2nd of June, 1995, Commander Hasanagic, on the basis of the assessment of the new developments and in order to use the Mujahedin Detachment forces, makes a proposal to the corps commander, to the division commander, that the detachment remains in his area of responsibility of the 35th Division; that's what it says here?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: I think that the proposal is quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Do you agree that it says "500 fighters" here?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that it says that here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: A little while ago, we saw this figure. That's why I made you focus on that, "350 to 400 soldiers," and here it says "500 soldiers." So it would seem that there is not a clear picture about the El Mudjahedin Detachment, because the Corps has one figure and the 35th Division has another figure for the strength of that detachment, and this is a substantial discrepancy, 100 to 150 people?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And if I may add, the exact number -- the exact strength of the El Mudjahedin Detachment could never be determined. I can give you an example, if you would allow me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: If they made any demands for food supplies, it would be quite natural, if you ask for cans, you ask for quantities sufficient for 100 to 150 soldiers, but it is not quite the usual practice to be asking for 200 to 300 soldiers. I don't know if I explained this clearly to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is just an example?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's just an example, but I heard of such cases. On one occasion, they asked for something without giving a precise strength, number of troops.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But under those circumstances, is it not possible that some people may be off duty and that's why food is not being ordered for them? I would imagine this would happen in any army.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the BH Army units, it was always known what the strength of the unit was at any given time, so people who were present and those who were absent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That is true, but when you ordered food for a unit of the Army of BiH, you wouldn't order food for those who are off duty and have gone away. You would order food for the number that is there. You wouldn't order food for the full strength of the unit, but you'd order food for the people who are present, unless I don't understand what you mean by ordering food.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this is just an example, but if you order food for 150 soldiers, then that's 150 soldiers who are present in the unit and who are supposed to get this food. You don't order for 150 to 200 soldiers. So you always knew who was there, who was supposed to get food, and we could never -- you could never just guess whether you would have 150 or 200 people. That's how it was in other BH Army units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And did you have to guess when you ordered food for the El Mudjahedin Detachment or did you give a specific amount of food for the number that is presently on duty at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can't give you an answer to that because I wasn't engaged in those duties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then your example doesn't work, because you were not engaged in those duties. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What I want to ask you is the following: You didn't have data, information, about this unit, because it appears here that the Corps has the information indicating that the strength of the detachment was less than the information that the Division had.

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: I've told you already that we never were able to determine the actual strength of that unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were unable to do so because the relationship between the 35th Division, as the superior unit, and the El Mujahedin, as the subordinate unit, was not such -- it was not a relationship in which one party was superior to the other and the other was subordinate, it was not the kind of relationship where you would get this kind of information from them; am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I want to ask you the following: You saw several documents about the communication between the El Mudjahedin Detachment and the Division Command, including the one that we've just seen, E583, that you yourself drafted, that dealt with the briefing to the chief of the Military Security Service in the 3rd Corps. You remember that document?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor showed you one specific segment that had to do with the El Mudjahedin Detachment. What you did write there, as you indicated: "The command and control system was not complied with." Do you recall having written that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then on the next page, you say that this unit achieved military successes. Are we then talking about the situation where this unit achieved those successes bypassing the Command and the chain-of-command system in the 35th Division, in fact it did not obey orders from the 35th Division? Did you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were such activities on their part, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, you asked, at the end of that question, "Did you understand my question," and the witness answered, "Yes." And that question is not transcribed. So the "yes" seems to be answering the former question, not answering whether he understood. Can we clear that, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I first asked you whether you understand my question. You said that you do. And now let me ask you the question again just to make everything clear for the record. My conclusion is that the El Mudjahedin Detachment, when it achieved its military successes, did not operate under the command of the 35th Division but under its own command. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to the form of the question, "my conclusion is that ..." and then I know Madam Vidovic is allowed to ask leading questions, but I think this again appears to be her testifying, it's her conclusion. I would just object to the form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is not examination-in-chief, this is cross-examination, and I am entitled to put anything to the witness in the most direct terms, to put my case to the witness, and that's what I do, that's what I did. And the witness now can either agree with what I put to him or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Madam Vidovic, but you cannot draw or present any of your own conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I will rephrase the question in this manner:

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Am I right if I believe that the El Mudjahedin Detachment, when it achieved its military successes, operated under its own command, the command of its own commanders and bosses, not the 35th Division? Could you please assist us in this regard?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: May I explain? The El Mudjahedin Detachment was given its tasks in the documents -- in the document signed by the commander of the 35th Division, but in the field, during the action itself, as far as I know, their commanders, if I may call them that, made their own decisions. They decided when to start the action, how they intended to go about it, and in such a situation the 35th Division Command did not have much influence. So, in other words, in the field they made their own decisions and they were not influenced by the 35th Division commander. That's as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we just understand? The decisions they made in the field, were they aimed at achieving the tasks that were given by the 35th Division or were they aimed at achieving other tasks that were not given by the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The essence is the following: They carried out each and every task in their own way, and they paid no heed to the orders of the commander of the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You described in the briefing the military success of the unit, and then you went on to describe the flip side, the incidents that they had been causing. And now I would like to ask you the following: Do you agree with me that those incidents were, in fact, the result of the fact that they had a different religion, a different view of life, because you described that they didn't allow women to swim, that they didn't want men and women to socialise and so on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Madam Vidovic. I just don't understand how that has to do with achieving tasks on the field. Are they having women in the field now? Surely, they -- I don't understand. I don't understand how you link those two.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may be of some assistance, I'm trying to get something clear about this document that the witness testified about. I want to find out what kind of incidents he actually reported to the 3rd Corps Command. He described the attacks on women, on people swimming or bathing, on -- that's E583, and that's the context in which I mentioned women, just because the witness mentions them in the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So do you agree that this is the kind of incidents that you describe --

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- to the superior command?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: If I may explain something, like the negative side of it. When we're talking about the women, these women were the mothers, the wives, the sisters of the BH Army fighters manning the defence lines, and quite naturally they worried about their families while they were up there on the front line, and this kind of incidents affected their combat morale and everything else.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. But I want to ask you the following: Do you agree that you did not describe in your report any killings or mistreatment of prisoners of war, killing of other people that they would have committed; you didn't have any such information and you did not include it in this report, is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: No, this was just information about the incidents that did not have any tragic consequences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Madam Vidovic. The witness -- has the witness testified about killing? I remember him testifying about the capture of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am trying to establish what kind of information the 35th Division had and what kind of information it forwarded to its superior command, and that is why I asked the witness quite specifically whether he actually had this kind of information about any killings or mistreatment of prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is a fact that you didn't have any such information?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't have any such information.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you did not report that to the superior command; is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, I'll ask you, when you answer, to please answer verbally rather than nodding your head, because when you nod the head, it doesn't get recorded on the transcript. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honour, I forgot to ask for an exhibit number for the document that we had a little while ago. That's D570. Could we have an exhibit number for that, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we give it a number, Madam Vidovic, you'll remember we mentioned that the dates are different within the two versions, and I notice also that the English version has a lot of "Illegible,""illegible," "illegible." You know, words were not read. And now that you say you've got a good copy, can you please find a fully-translated English version. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 589.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you something else about the El Mudjahedin Detachment. Do you agree that the commander of the 35th Division demanded any reports from the detachment on various issues, if you know?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: I assume that he did, because that unit was to be treated in the same way as any other unit in the 35th Division, and it was to have the same kind of obligations towards the 35th Division Command.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you for your sphere of work. Do you agree with me that the military security is quite peculiar, in that the subordination principle comes to the fore, to the greatest possible extent? In other words, there should be very close cooperation between the superior and subordinate units, and the chain of command, the subordination principle, should be complied with to the fullest possible extent; am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's how the service functions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So every unit subordinate to you should send its own security reports to you; is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if the El Mujahedin had a security organ, then it should have sent its reports to you; am I right?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now please tell the Trial Chamber whether you ever received any such report?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: One more thing. You had associates in the Military Security, in the lower-level units. You worked with those people on a daily basis; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any such person that you worked with in the El Mudjahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you ever able to give them any tasks, in terms of military security, to the commander or anybody else in that unit?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: No, I never managed to establish any kind of contact with them in this regard.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And let me just ask you a very brief question. The documents show that there is some knowledge about this detachment. Do you agree with me that the knowledge about the El Mudjahedin Detachment mostly came from other units of the BH Army; for instance, the 328th Brigade, so that you didn't get the information about them from them directly, but you got it from units that were adjacent to them?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, from the soldiers in the adjacent units who would see them in the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This also applied to their dead; is that so?

utterances.speaker: FADIL IMAMOVIC
utterances.text: Any information about them was obtained in this manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Your Honours, I think this is a convenient time for us to stop. Unfortunately, I didn't manage to finish my cross-examination because this witness is much too important for the Defence for us to cut his examination short to any considerable extent. I'm sorry for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, we are all sorry to you, because in this institution it is a public holiday tomorrow, so we will not be working, and it would have been good if we could have finished with you and let you go home before the weekend, but we are not able to do so. So you'll have to come back on Monday, the 15th of October, at 9.00 in the morning. Yes, at 9.00 in the morning, in this same courtroom. Okay? You understand? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You may stand down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Court adjourned to Monday, the 15th of October at 9.00 in the morning, Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 15th day of October, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24
